memory_candidates.content: On this harness, a foreground Bash call is auto-backgrounded after roughly 180s of output silence even when its own `timeout` parameter is raised far above that threshold (tested at 570000ms) -- the harness's silence heuristic, not the declared ceiling, triggers the detach. The reliable pattern for a genuinely long local verification battery (e.g. a 100+ suite narrowed run-all.sh invocation) is: launch with `setsid bash -c '... > logfile 2>&1; echo EXIT:$? >> logfile' < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 & disown`, capture the inner pid via `pgrep -af`, then poll with a `for i in $(seq 1 N); do sleep 10; kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break; done` loop kept under ~170s total per Bash call so the poll call itself is never auto-backgrounded. Never rely on the harness's own background-task notification to resume a dispatched subagent, since that path hands the dispatch back unfinished.

deploy-headless.sh's whole-tree orphan detection (gate 13) flags deployed-but-undeclared files (e.g. a deployed copy of a script just deleted from the source store) but does not remove them on a failed verify -- it reports `RESULT=landed_verify_red` and leaves the orphan in place. The remedy is to remove the orphaned deployed-tree file explicitly (`.claude/**` is gitignored and disposable, so a direct `rm` is safe) and either re-run a scoped `verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 13,3,5 --skip-unchanged` for a fast confirmation or re-run `deploy-headless.sh` once more for the literal clean-verify record.

verify-touched.sh's suite-resolution for an edit to manifest.json or suite-classification.data (high-fan-in files many suites declare as corpus inputs) triggers a 100+ suite narrowed run-all.sh battery even at the plan's declared `interface` tier, not a handful of directly-dependent suites. Budget accordingly (10-20+ minutes under concurrent batch load) rather than assuming 'interface' implies a cheap check; a manifest/classification-data edit is itself the costly case this tier exists to catch.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code Bash tool auto-backgrounding
sapience_notes.value: A foreground Bash call on this harness is auto-backgrounded after roughly 180s of output silence regardless of the declared `timeout` parameter (confirmed at 570000ms); the only reliable way to wait out a long local command is to setsid-detach it to a log file and poll liveness via `kill -0` on the captured pid in short (<170s) loops, never relying on the harness's background-task notification to resume the dispatch.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh orphan handling
sapience_notes.value: deploy-headless.sh's whole-tree orphan detection (gate 13) flags a deployed-but-undeclared file left over from a source-store deletion, but does not remove it; a failed verify (landed_verify_red) with an orphan finding requires the deployed copy to be removed explicitly before a clean verify is achievable.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh suite-resolution fan-out
sapience_notes.value: Editing manifest.json or suite-classification.data (declared corpus inputs for many suites) causes verify-touched.sh to select a 100+ suite narrowed battery even at the plan's declared 'interface' verification tier, costing 10-20+ minutes under concurrent batch load rather than a handful of directly-dependent checks.

sapience_notes.subject: gate-lock mutex staleness window
sapience_notes.value: The shared gate-lock mutex (/run/user/1000/.gate-lock, used to serialize gate-8/verify-deploy runs) has a 1800s staleness window; a crashed holder's dead PID does not release the lock faster than that window elapsing, so a bounded wait shorter than 1800s can time out on a stale lock even after confirming the holder process is already dead via kill -0.

sapience_notes.subject: milestone-ref-land.sh deletion rationale
sapience_notes.value: A documentation reference to a dead utility (not just a live code caller) can itself be the invocation vector for unexplained system behavior -- this task treated re-pointing the ref-plumbing pattern's two context documents as part of the fix, not cosmetic cleanup, specifically because the task description's leading hypothesis for a consumer repository's unexplained ref advances was an agent reading one of those documents and running the deleted script by hand.
